name: Fota Arboretum
title: Ancient Trees in Cork's Fota Arboretum: 7 to Find
meta_description: A Smith-Barry family collection on an island in Cork Harbour, mild enough to grow palms and camphor trees outdoors at Newfoundland's latitude.
intro: Fota Island sits at the same latitude as Newfoundland, and the only reason its arboretum can grow a Canary Island date palm and a camphor tree from southern China outdoors is the Gulf Stream, which keeps this stretch of Cork Harbour close to frost-free. The Smith-Barry family began building the collection here in the 1820s on what had been ordinary farmland, and the national heritage tree survey's oldest find, a holm oak banded to 200 to 300 years, predates that start and would have already been standing when they began. The rest of the collection is younger and stranger: a Campbell's magnolia that covers itself in dinner-plate pink flowers for about ten days each late winter before it leafs at all; a Japanese cedar cultivar whose every needle grows in a tight curl, a Victorian nursery mutation nicknamed Granny's Ringlets; a New Zealand conifer with no true leaves, its flattened stem tissue notched enough to look like celery; and a coast redwood that in its native California would be the tallest tree species on Earth, here still a child of 150 to 200 years next to the two-thousand-year specimens back home. Free to visit, on the same island as Fota Wildlife Park.
